mac_setup_notes: Hardware: Apple M5 Max with 64 GB unified memory, 2 TB SSD, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md, "The machine"). A 64 GB M5 Max is the 40-core-GPU part, 614 GB/s, per apple.com/macbook-pro/specs (the 32-core part, 460 GB/s, comes only with 36 GB). Serving: Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 through the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. The page itself warns that the engine version changes results: gemma4:12b dropped from 5/5 to 1/5 on 0.33.0 with the same digest. Measured 22-23 August 2026 on the embedded SQLite sample, six surfaces, five consecutive passes each. Durations are whole agent runs (many turns), not tok/s, and are the median and slowest of the passing runs. Per-turn limit is 90 s (shipped default). None of the five lane models carries a 150 s override. Sampling defaults are temperature 0 and top_p 1, with an unreported-call ceiling of 12, one report reminder and one present reminder. A model with no tuning entry also gets one plan-statement ask and one unread-stop answer (model-tuning.md). Per model: qwen2.5:7b got one plan ask but never used it. qwen2.5:14b ran at pure defaults. qwen2.5:32b needs the one plan ask, and without it the plan cell is 4/5. qwen2.5-coder:14b got one plan ask but never used it. qwq:32b ran at defaults with nothing configured. Context: the pages do not record OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, num_ctx, KV cache type, flash attention or per-turn prompt sizes. Ollama's default context depends on memory size, so the Mac runs probably used a much larger default than the 4k Ollama gives on a GPU under 24 GiB here (inference, not recorded). Thinking: no think or reasoning setting is recorded for these five. suppressAgentReasoning and suppressPlanReasoning default to false, so qwq:32b reasoned on every turn. Tool protocol: Studio falls back to a prose tool protocol when an endpoint lacks native tool calling, and decides this per endpoint (setup.md:95, testing-your-own.md:15). So a pass shows the model is reliable in Studio's guarded loop. It does not by itself prove native tool_calls emission. Sustained-load caveat: lost cells were re-measured on a rested machine. The authors call every timing a best case and the pass/fail column the transferable part. Doc drift: methodology.md says six models carry 150 s and "the other sixteen" keep 90, while README.md says nine of fifty-one. This does not affect this lane.

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights 4.36 GiB. f16 KV is 56 KiB/token (28 x 4 x 128 x 2 x 2 B): 32k = 1.75 GiB, 64k = 3.5 GiB, 128k = 7 GiB. Weights plus 64k f16 KV plus about 0.5-1 GiB compute is about 8.5-9 GiB, well under 15.47 GiB. 128k f16 is about 12 GiB and still fits. No CPU offload, and system RAM needs only a few GiB. Caveat: the GGUF is trained to 32,768 and carries no YaRN metadata. Ollama's OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 alone does not enable YaRN, so OpenCode's 64k floor needs llama.cpp with explicit --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 2 (or 4) --yarn-orig-ctx 32768. Whether Ollama clamps num_ctx to 32768 for this model was not verified.
models.best_runtime_here: Two runtimes, depending on the job. For reproducing the libredb harness, use Ollama, because the evidence is engine-specific and should match the Ollama 0.33.0 the Mac used. Set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH to at least 32768 instead of the 4k default; the harness's own prompt sizes are unrecorded. For OpenCode, use llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1, --jinja (Hermes-style Qwen2.5 tool format), -ngl 99 -fa on, and -c 65536 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 2 --yarn-orig-ctx 32768. vLLM would need an AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit build, because the BF16 build is about 15 GB, plus --tool-call-parser hermes. There is no reason to prefer it here.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: faster (estimate). The model fits fully in VRAM, so decode is bandwidth-bound: 896/614 = about 1.46x the M5 Max ceiling, roughly 190 vs 130 tok/s theoretical. TechFuelHQ measured 177-180 tok/s on the desktop 5080 at 960 GB/s (third-party), so expect about 160-170 here if clocks hold at 140 W. Prefill on the RTX should beat the Mac by more than decode does. Whole-run times are therefore likely at or below the Mac's 6 s median, but that is not a conversion of the run numbers.
models.opencode_suitability: Native tools (Ollama 'tools' badge; Hermes tool format, vLLM hermes parser). No thinking mode. Native context is 32k, so the 64k OpenCode floor needs static YaRN, which may cost quality on short prompts per the Qwen card. libredb evidence: 30/30 consecutive passes with no tuning needed. That is strong evidence of reliable tool calls in a guarded, short-context SQL tool loop. It does not show multi-file coding or long-context behaviour. As an OpenCode main agent it is a 2024 7B with no modern agentic scores, so treat it as a fast sub-agent or small-model backend at most.
models.reason: Cheapest and lowest-risk cross-check of the user's harness on this GPU. It fits fully in VRAM with room for 64k or more of KV, should run faster than on the Mac, and is the roster's fastest and steadiest small model. Try it first for the libredb use case. For OpenCode it is limited by the 32k native context and its age.

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights 8.37 GiB. KV is 192 KiB/token at f16 (48 x 8 x 128 x 2 x 2 B). At 32k: f16 is 6 GiB, about 14.9 GiB total, which is too tight. q8_0 is about 3.2 GiB, about 12.1 GiB total, which fits. At 64k: f16 is 12 GiB and does not fit. q8_0 is about 6.4 GiB, about 15.3-15.8 GiB with compute, which is at or over the 15.47 GiB CUDA limit, and Ollama would push a few layers to the CPU. q4_0 is about 3.4 GiB, about 12.3 GiB total, which fits. At 48k with q8_0, about 13.7 GiB fits. Beyond 32k also needs YaRN, which Ollama does not apply from this GGUF. Ollama needs OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 or q4_0 (server-wide) to quantize the KV cache. RAM need is small if it stays on the GPU. TechFuelHQ measured 13,159 MiB whole-GPU at 16k f16 on Ollama (third-party, desktop).
models.best_runtime_here: For the libredb harness, use Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0. That keeps it fully on the GPU on the engine family the evidence comes from. For OpenCode at 64k, use llama.cpp b12407 with GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1, --jinja, -ngl 99 -fa on, -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 (or q8_0 at about 48k) and -c 65536 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 2 --yarn-orig-ctx 32768. Check nvidia-smi for spill. vLLM with an AWQ build (about 9.4 GiB) would leave too little KV room after vLLM's roughly 2 GiB reserve for 64k.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: faster while it stays fully in VRAM (estimate): 896/614 is about 1.46x the decode ceiling, roughly 107 vs 73 tok/s theoretical. TechFuelHQ measured 94.5-97 tok/s on the desktop 5080, so expect about 85-90 here. If 64k q8_0 KV forces Ollama to put a few layers on the CPU, decode drops sharply, so keep KV small enough to stay resident. Whole-run times are not converted.
models.opencode_suitability: Native tools ('tools' badge, Hermes format), no thinking, 32k native and 64k only through YaRN plus quantized KV. libredb evidence: 30/30 at pure defaults, so tool calling in a guarded loop is reliable without per-model tuning. The tail is a single slow Assess cell (1:03). Old (2024) with no modern agentic-coding scores, so it is weaker than the KB's Qwen3.x picks for OpenCode.
models.reason: First-hand 30/30 tool reliability at defaults, and it fits fully in VRAM at 32k with q8_0 KV and should run faster than on the Mac. But 64k needs YaRN plus q4_0 KV, and it is a generation behind the KB picks, so it is a libredb backend candidate more than an OpenCode one.

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights 18.49 GiB against 15.47 GiB of CUDA memory, so it cannot fit even at 4k. KV is 256 KiB/token at f16 (64 x 8 x 128 x 2 x 2 B): 64k = 16 GiB at f16 and about 8.5 GiB at q8_0. models.speed_here_vs_mac: much slower (estimate). On the Mac all 18.5 GiB are read at 614 GB/s (about 31 tok/s ceiling). Here about half the weights are read from DDR5 (102.4 GB/s peak, realistic 60-80 GB/s), so decode is about 5-8 tok/s, roughly 3-4x slower. Prefill for the CPU-resident layers is also far slower. The Mac's 20 s median and 36 s worst runs would stretch to minutes, and long turns could approach the 90 s per-turn limit.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools yes, no thinking, 32k native. libredb shows 30/30, but only with the plan ask. Not practical for OpenCode here: 64k of KV plus offload makes it slow, and newer models in the KB (Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) dominate it.
models.reason: Dense 18.5 GiB weights spill about half the model into DDR5. The Mac result does not transfer in speed, it needs a tuning entry to pass, and qwen2.5:14b matches it on the same harness while fitting in VRAM.

Label it '(measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio)' and note: Ollama 0.32.13/0.33.0, a 90 s per-turn limit, whole-run durations rather than tok/s, and a guarded loop with reminders and a possible prose-tool fallback. No model in this lane is in the KB's ranking, honorable mentions or exclusions, so the harness covers none of the KB's top 10 from this lane. Consider qwen2.5:7b, and possibly qwen2.5:14b, as a 'fast tool-calling sub-agent / libredb backend' note rather than a ranked OpenCode pick. qwen2.5:7b passed 30/30 at the fastest times on the Mac and fits fully in VRAM with 64k+ of KV (estimate about 9 GiB at 64k f16).

Record a context caveat the KB does not yet have. Qwen2.5 GGUFs on Ollama carry qwen2.context_length 32768 and no YaRN keys, verified by GGUF header read. Setting OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 does not enable YaRN. OpenCode's 64k floor (docs/opencode.md:190) for these models needs llama.cpp --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 2 --yarn-orig-ctx 32768, or vLLM static YaRN, and the Qwen card warns of quality loss on short texts.

Record the conflict on qwen2.5-coder:14b in docs/community-benchmarks.md:301. TechFuelHQ on Ollama with an RTX 5080 says it failed the Tools task. libredb says 30/30 first-attempt passes. Note that Studio decides native vs prose tool protocol per endpoint (libredb setup.md:95), so the two results measure different things, and the KB should not claim either 'qwen2.5-coder tools broken' or 'reliable' without a native tool_calls probe here.

Nuance docs/opencode.md:201. The claim that small models fail agent loops through malformed or missing tool calls is about 2B-4B. The libredb harness shows a 7B (qwen2.5:7b) and even 4B models (qwen3:4b, qwen3.5:4b, outside this lane) passing 30/30 in a short-context, guarded SQL tool loop. That does not refute the OpenCode claim, whose long contexts and free-form edits are harder, but the sentence should say it refers to OpenCode-style loops.

Confirm the KB's runtime guidance. These are dense models, so --n-cpu-moe does not apply. For the 32B dense models neither Ollama nor llama.cpp avoids the DDR5 bottleneck, which supports keeping dense 32B models out of the picks as was done for Devstral.

The TechFuelHQ desktop 5080 rows already in community-benchmarks.md (qwen2.5:7b 177-180 tok/s, :14b 94-97, coder:14b 93-95) can serve as the expected ceiling when these tags are measured here. Expect about 5-10% lower on the 896 GB/s laptop at 140 W (estimate).
